title: Passion Night: Upper Room, Gethsemane & Hearings
subtitle: Jerusalem, Kidron, Mount of Olives, and unresolved hearing locations
summary: Explore the physical setting of the Last Supper and Gethsemane narratives, then the unresolved Annas/Caiaphas hearing geography, without inventing an upper-room building, arrest route, garden boundary, or priestly residence.
disclaimer: The Gospels place the Last Supper in Jerusalem, Gethsemane across the Kidron toward the Mount of Olives, and subsequent hearings in Jerusalem, but they do not provide a recoverable street-by-street route, the original upper-room building, the exact garden boundary/arrest point, or a securely identified Annas/Caiaphas hearing building. Display anchors used here are navigation aids, not recovered event locations.

evidenceLegend.description: Established topography or measured terrain when a verified DEM is configured.

evidenceLegend.label: Known archaeology
evidenceLegend.description: Archaeological context represented only at the level supported by existing atlas records.

evidenceLegend.label: Historical inference
evidenceLegend.description: A historically reasoned reconstruction or orientation that is not an observed event location.

entryCamera.note: This camera frames central Jerusalem, the Kidron depression, and the Mount of Olives as a geographic relationship; it is not an event coordinate.

hotspots.label: Upper room — exact building unknown
hotspots.summary: The Synoptic accounts place the meal in a prepared upper room in Jerusalem without identifying a recoverable building.

whyShown.evidence: The Gospel text locates the meal within Jerusalem, but not in a uniquely identifiable structure.
whyShown.inference: The marker is a display anchor within the city used to orient the user before the eastward movement.
whyShown.alternatives: Later Cenacle tradition is historically important but is not treated as proof of the original room.

hotspots.label: Kidron Valley
hotspots.summary: The Kidron is an established physical valley between Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives; John explicitly places movement across the Kidron before the garden episode.

whyShown.evidence: The valley is a durable geographic feature and the text names the Kidron crossing.
whyShown.inference: No exact first-century path across the valley is reconstructed.

hotspots.label: Mount of Olives ridge
hotspots.summary: The Mount of Olives is established physical geography east of Jerusalem and provides the broad setting for Gethsemane.

whyShown.evidence: The ridge is securely identified geographic terrain named in the Passion sequence.
whyShown.inference: The scene does not infer an exact path, property line, or tree location from the modern landscape.

hotspots.label: Gethsemane — traditional area
hotspots.summary: The Gospel setting at the Mount of Olives is strong, while the modern garden enclosure is a later traditional localization.

whyShown.evidence: The Synoptic Gospels name Gethsemane and John describes a garden across the Kidron.
whyShown.inference: The atlas record uses the traditional area as an orientation point, not as proof of the exact first-century boundary.
whyShown.alternatives: The exact garden extent and arrest point remain unrecoverable.

hotspots.label: Exact arrest point — not recoverable
hotspots.summary: The narratives describe an arrest in the Gethsemane/garden setting, but no archaeological method can identify the exact spot.

whyShown.evidence: The event belongs to the narrative sequence, not to an independently recoverable point.
whyShown.inference: This is a display anchor beside the traditional Gethsemane orientation so the interface can explain what remains unknown.

hotspots.label: Annas / Caiaphas hearings — building unlocated
hotspots.summary: The Passion narratives place hearings involving Annas and/or Caiaphas in Jerusalem, but the atlas does not identify a modern pilgrimage house as the proven hearing location.

whyShown.evidence: The hearings are part of the textual Jerusalem sequence, but the texts do not provide a recoverable modern building coordinate.
whyShown.inference: This southern/western Jerusalem point is a display anchor only so the unresolved hearing geography can be discussed after the arrest.
whyShown.alternatives: Later House of Caiaphas pilgrimage traditions are not promoted to established event geography.
